If the outermost subdomain

the case-insensitive subdomain match determines which of the six is used; HTTP is the fallback

candidateAdjudications.reason: The span straddles a verb ('matches') and a comma-separated list of established protocol names, so it is not a noun pile. 'Outermost subdomain name' is a clear three-word phrase and the protocol names are component identities.

In 'otherwise it assumes HTTP' only an agent capable of inference can be the subject, which restricts the referent to curl; the other nearby nouns (URL, protocol, subdomain name) yield incoherent readings rather than competing meanings.

This sits in a paragraph describing curl's scheme-guessing behaviour, and the 'by' phrase supplies a means ('providing a full URL'), not a hidden agent. It is a capability statement rather than an instruction, so no actor is concealed.

The passive is in a subordinate clause describing where curl sends output; the main clause is already an active imperative ('use the --output or the --remote-name options'). The writing agent is curl and is irrelevant to the reader's action.
The genuine noun phrase is 'dedicated destination option', which is transparent; the span only reaches four words by swallowing the conjunction 'unless' that begins the next clause.
Descriptive prose about platform behaviour, and the agent is already named explicitly ('by the operating system'). The reader is not the actor and nothing is hidden.

'curl can be told to download URLs' is a version-scoped capability statement with curl as the topic, not an instruction; the implied teller is the reader and is obvious from the surrounding option reference.
The span crosses a comma between a text file and one URL per line; these are separate, ordinary phrases.

'It is done with `--url @filename`' takes the whole just-described operation as its referent; the competing nouns (text file, URL, line) all give incoherent readings, so there is only one sustainable resolution.

Agentless in form, but the same sentence supplies the active restatement immediately after the colon ('you specify a filename prefixed with the `@` symbol'), so the actor is explicit within the passage and nothing is concealed.

The referent is curl, echoing 'curl can be told' two sentences earlier; the carried-over reading from the preceding 'It is done' points at the `--url @filename` mechanism, but both readings send the reader to the same action, so the choice does not change the meaning. Marginal call.

Same construction as the earlier 'curl can be told': a capability statement about the tool in descriptive reference prose, with the means stated ('by providing an argument like `@-`') and the implied teller obvious.
